messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: serving-runtime group: elevated CUDA OOM + illegal memory access errors on nodes gpu-27/gpu-28. 5xx spike observed for /v1/generate. Auto-rollback attempted for recent runtime reload.
maria-oncall: I'm on it. paging in. seeing alert graphs in console, latency up ~3x for a subset of requests. starting triage.
raj-ml: pinging in case this is the quantized loader change I ran yesterday. any rollout info?
maria-oncall: @raj-ml we rolled a new loader flag on dedicated pool at 03:04 UTC — small canary then ramp. metrics show error spike right at 03:09.
sam-runtime: oncall takeover in 3m. tagging @maria-oncall to handoff. I'm running `kubectl -n runtime get pods -l pool=dedicated-gpu -o wide` now.
maria-oncall: handing to @sam-runtime — I attached initial notes below, I'll stay on until handoff completes.

maria-oncall: logs from gpu-27 container (recent):
```
[2026-03-14T03:09:07Z] serving-runtime[pid=2141]: GPU0: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS at 0x7f8a12bff000
[2026-03-14T03:09:07Z] serving-runtime[pid=2141]: stacktrace: runtime/loader.cpp:512 handle_eviction
[2026-03-14T03:09:08Z] kernel: eviction: pagewalk fault on device 0, code 0x50
[2026-03-14T03:09:09Z] nvidia-driver[530.41]: WARNING: misaligned vaddr detected during pagewalk
```

sam-runtime: thanks. looks like misaligned pagewalk/kernel-level issue rather than pure OOM. but OOMs are co-occurring (paging pressure). I'm going to cordon gpu-27 and drain pods that hit illegal address to stop user impact.
sam-runtime: `kubectl cordon node/gpu-27 && kubectl drain node/gpu-27 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m`

deploy-bot: deploy status: recent runtime reload (flag: loader-quantize=true) completed at 03:06 UTC to dedicated gpu pool (50% ramp). Canary targets passed internal health checks but errors started after ramp.

raj-ml: if it's the loader change, fallback to previous loader would be fastest. any safe fallback we can trigger without full rollback?
sam-runtime: we have a fallback route in the console: route `dedicated-gpu` has variant `compat-v1` (no quantize loader). I'll flip to compat-v1 for the affected tiles for quick mitigation.

maria-oncall: customer impact: CS triage indicates ~12 customers saw 502/503s in the 03:09–03:14 window. one enterprise customer reported degraded throughput in logs. notifying @julie-cs.
julie-cs: acknowledged — sending templated blurb to affected customers: "We've seen transient errors impacting generation latency and availability; engineers are mitigating and will follow up."

sam-runtime: mitigation step 1: toggled route to compat-v1 for `dedicated-gpu` at 03:12 UTC. traffic shifted, error rate dropped from 18% -> 2% by 03:14. leaving canary open for 15m.

sam-runtime: mitigation step 2: cordoned gpu-27 and gpu-28; drained pods that had repeated illegal access traces. moving workloads to fresh nodes.
maria-oncall: observed some containers crashlooping with `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` after reload. saving core dumps and callstacks to /var/logs/incidents/4443216789.

raj-ml: quick repro hypothesis: certain high-seq-length requests + loader-quantize path triggers misaligned KVCACHE pointer on reload under paging pressure. possible race where page table entries are torn during on-demand pagewalks.
sam-runtime: agree. for immediate hotfix we should: 1) keep compat-v1 enabled; 2) avoid reloading affected pods; 3) pin driver to 528.x on repro nodes and test; 4) collect perf traces.

maria-oncall: I've started a kernel-level capture on gpu-27 (ftrace enabled) and uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-incident-dumps/4443216789/ftrace.tgz
sam-runtime: can someone run a quick replicate on a repro cluster? `make reproduce-oom` in runtime/test-harness triggers similar behavior in staging with loader-quantize=true.

raj-ml: running reproduce now in staging, will post results. if we can reproduce under a controlled page-swap emulator we can validate a kernel patch.

sam-runtime: next steps for oncall: keep compat-v1 for 2 hours, monitor latency and errors. if stable, schedule controlled rollout pause for the loader change and open a follow-up: infra/driver-team to triage NV driver interactions.
maria-oncall: handing to @sam-runtime for postmortem. I'm un-paging. good job team. :thumbsup:
sam-runtime: taking over. I'll coordinate debug, create incident bridge, and file ticket with driver vendor if kernel traces point to pagewalk race. assigning followups.

sam-runtime: incident bridge: https://zoom.internal/incident/4443216789
sam-runtime: filing P1 ticket in tracker: RINF-INC-4443216789. initial labels: gpu, cuda-illegal, paging, regression-loader.

raj-ml: staging repro shows deterministic illegal access when we interleave large-seq requests + rapid reload of KV cache: attaching minimal repro script to ticket.

julie-cs: I'll send updated customer follow-ups in 30m with ETA: "We have mitigations active, monitoring; next update in 60 minutes with root-cause status."

sam-runtime: summary for post-incident: suspected kernel pagewalk race triggered by new loader path under paging pressure -> illegal device addresses & OOM cascades -> container crashes and node flaps -> customer 5xxs. Immediate mitigation: route fallback to compat-v1, cordon/drain affected nodes, pin reloads.
sam-runtime: tagging: @raj-ml for repro + fix, @maria-oncall for logs, @deploy-bot to keep rollout paused, @julie-cs for customer comms.

sam-runtime: closing handoff note. last check 03:20 UTC error rate stable at 0.9%. will keep bridge open for root cause work.
